findings.explanation: c3 and c4 separately report completing tasks 5–7 [M5][M6], explicitly confirmed as done by both in [M7]. They also deliver different-sized task-4 implementations to the same gates.txt path [M10][M13]. These are repeated implementation deliveries, not merely independent verification; the verification claims concern their respective outputs.

Conflicting allocations give tasks 4 and 5–7 to different owners [M2][M4], followed by both agents' completion claims [M5][M6][M10][M13]. Task-3 ownership also remains unsettled: c3 asks whether c2 is optimizing [M12]; c2 requests no edits and restores passing plans [M15][M16], yet c3 reports overwriting them and asks c2 not to regenerate [M17]. No accepted final owner or version is visible.

Both agents' completion of tasks 5–7 is explicitly visible in [M5][M6] and consolidated in [M7], but the later directive [M8] assigns those tasks again without acknowledging completion or specifying verification. That is a clear opportunity to incorporate shared completion information. The later task-3 preservation requests and reported overwrite [M15][M16][M17] are additionally unresolved, though exact action timing is uncertain.
